messages.text: Why is Antonelli taking grid penalties on home soil in Italy?

metadata.summary: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is highly unlikely to be in contention for victory on home soil at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Kimi Antonelli: Why is Mercedes driver taking grid penalties at Italian Grand Prix in Monza on home soil? | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Kimi Antonelli: Why is Mercedes driver taking grid penalties at Italian Grand Prix in Monza on home soil? Kimi Antonelli could lose ground in the championship this weekend as he will start from the back in Sunday's Italian Grand Prix; watch every session of the Italian GP live on Sky Sports, starting with Friday's practice sessions at 11.30am and 3pm Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Friday 28 August 2026 12:58, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on The F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins believes Mercedes have 'front-loaded' their upgrades following Toto Wolff admitting his team 'haven't got the money' to match their rivals' upgrades Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is highly unlikely to be in contention for victory on home soil at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix. Antonelli will start at the back of the grid as he will exceed the limit of four power units that can be used in a season before incurring grid penalties. It means the Mercedes driver could see his 59-point lead over team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton cut significantly, while a third consecutive win for McLaren's Lando Norris could enable the reigning world champion to make major inroads into his 83-point deficit to Antonelli. metadata.summary: Carlos Alcaraz impressed on his return to tennis with a straight-sets win over Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first round of the US Open.
metadata.content: US Open 2026: Carlos Alcaraz impresses on return from injury as Aryna Sabalenka, Harriet Dart also win | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open 2026: Carlos Alcaraz impresses on return from injury as Aryna Sabalenka, Harriet Dart also win Defending champions Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka comfortably came through their first-round matches; Alcaraz was playing his first singles match since April; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Tuesday 1 September 2026 05:37, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open first-round match between Roman Safiullin and Carlos Alcaraz Carlos Alcaraz impressed on his return to tennis with a straight-sets win over Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first round of the US Open. Alcaraz has not played a competitive singles match since withdrawing from the Barcelona Open in April with a wrist injury that forced him to miss the French Open and Wimbledon. The severity of the injury, which did not require surgery, meant Alcaraz was a doubt for the US Open but he entered Flushing Meadows and showed with his 6-4 6-4 6-4 win over Safiullin that he cannot be dismissed from defending his title from last year. metadata.summary: Aryna Sabalenka hit back at her critics, saying "haters can go and get on with their own lives" after she made a winning start in her quest for a ‌third successive US Open title.
metadata.content: US Open: Aryna Sabalenka ‘tired of the miserable haters’ as she hits back at critics after first-round win | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open: Aryna Sabalenka ‘tired of the miserable haters’ as she hits back at critics after first-round win Aryna Sabalenka hits back at her critics after an opening victory over Colombia's Camila ​Osorio at Flushing Meadows; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app Tuesday 1 September 2026 06:34, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aryna Sabalenka hits back at critics, saying she is tired of the negativity surrounding her with everything she does both on and off the court Aryna Sabalenka hit back at her critics, saying "haters can go and get on with their own lives" after she made a winning start in her quest for a ‌third successive US Open title. Sabalenka is attempting to regain her usual dominance after a frustrating last six months, ​having failed to reach a final since she completed the Sunshine Double in March, but she made a confident start to her quest for a ‌rare 'three-peat' at the year's final major. The world No 1 launched 32 winners to defeat Camila Osorio 6-2 6-4 in the first match of the day ‌on Arthur Ashe Stadium to set up a meeting with Russia's Polina Iatcenko in the second round. The Northern Irishman finished in a seven-way tie for fourth at the FedEx Cup over the weekend, finishing five shots off tournament winner Scottie Scheffler despite showing earlier signs of promise. Now 37, six-time major winner McIlroy admitted his "fuse was shorter than it used to be" before the final round at the East Lake Golf Club. Image: Rory McIlroy has admitted his patience with the demands of professional golf is thinning He had arrived in Atlanta off the back of three weeks of competing in a row, something he admitted he would never exceed again despite still managing a fourth-place finish over the weekend. metadata.summary: Derek McInnes' immediate touchline ban has been reduced following Rangers' appeal.
metadata.content: Derek McInnes: Rangers manager's touchline ban changed after appeal over 'disgusting' comment last season | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Derek McInnes: Rangers manager's touchline ban changed after appeal over 'disgusting' comment last season Rangers appealed the four-match ban handed to Derek McInnes; former Hearts boss described the awarding of a penalty to Celtic at Motherwell as "disgusting"; McInnes will now serve an immediate two-match touchline ban instead of three after appeal hearing Sahil Jaidka Scotland Bureau Editor @SahilJaidka Monday 31 August 2026 22:24, UK Image: Derek McInnes' immediate touchline ban has been reduced Derek McInnes' immediate touchline ban has been reduced following Rangers' appeal. The 55-year-old was initially handed a four-match suspension by the Scottish FA, with three of those games to be served immediately. While the overall ban remains in place, he will now only serve two of those with immediate effect, while the other two will only be triggered should he breach disciplinary rule 72 again before the end of this season. As part of disciplinary rule 72 you can not: (i) criticise the decision(s) and/or performance(s) of any or all match official(s) in such a way as to indicate bias or incompetence on the part of such match official; or (ii) make remarks about such match official(s) which impinge on his character Got Sky? messages.text: Is now the right time for Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' US Open loss?

metadata.summary: Novak Djokovic said he "despised" every moment of the five-set, near five-hour ordeal which ended his US Open hopes in the first round, so now the question is whether he calls time on his trophy-laden career.
metadata.content: US Open: Is now the right time for Novak Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' first-round exit in New York? | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content Opinion US Open: Is now the right time for Novak Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' first-round exit in New York? Novak Djokovic will turn 40 next May and after his shock exit in New York there is talk that the former world No 1 should call time on his career; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app By Raz Mirza at Flushing Meadows, New York Monday 31 August 2026 23:27, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gigi Salmon is joined by Tim Henman and Ryan Harrison to debate whether Novak Djokovic should consider retirement after ongoing health issues and a shock first-round exit at the 2026 US Open Novak Djokovic said he "despised" every moment of the five-set, near five-hour ordeal which ended his US Open hopes in the first round, so now the question is whether he calls time on his trophy-laden career. The 24-time Grand Slam champion was knocked out in the first round of the US Open for the first time, beaten by Mariano Navone of Argentina . Djokovic was 19-0 in the US Open first round and hadn't lost his opening match in any major since Paul Goldstein beat him at the Australian Open in 2006.
